title: Solar Self-Consumption Ratio Dip
dataSources: SolarEdge/Enphase production (`solaredge:power`, `enphase:production`), Powerwall (`powerwall:aggregate`), smart-meter P1/DSMR (`dsmr:telegram`), Emporia Vue (`emporia:circuit`).
app: Solar inverters (SolarEdge/Enphase/Fronius/Growatt), Tesla Powerwall, and smart meters (P1/DSMR, Emporia Vue, Sense) via vendor APIs and MQTT to HEC.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=powerwall:aggregate
| bin _time span=1d
| stats sum(solar_kw) as solar_kw, sum(eval(if(grid_kw<0,abs(grid_kw),0))) as export_kw by _time
| eval self_consumed_pct=round(100*(solar_kw-export_kw)/solar_kw,1)
| where solar_kw>0 AND self_consumed_pct<60
| sort self_consumed_pct
description: Estimates how much of your solar production stayed useful at home versus being exported, surfacing days where self-consumption fell off a cliff.
value: Self-consumption is where the bill savings live; a dip can point to scheduling opportunities, battery settings, or simply habits worth shifting.
implementation: Forward site power-flow telemetry from Powerwall or a similar gateway; review daily self-consumption percentage and tune loads accordingly.
visualization: Daily chart of solar generation versus estimated export and self-consumption percentage.
grandmaExplanation: It watches how much of your solar power you actually used yourself instead of sending back out to the grid.
